e1e5a650abb7aebe014d5a46458706fea6baa018.title: Jackson factorial upper bound
e1e5a650abb7aebe014d5a46458706fea6baa018.body:
Assume that, for every finite observed law, the sample law is the canonical i.i.d. product law of \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}. Then there are universal tuning constants \(H_0>0\), \(\kappa\in(0,1)\), and an integer cutoff \(D_0>2\) such that the estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator} satisfies the following bound. For every overlap constant \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge 1\), every \(d\ge 2\), and every observed law \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) in \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class},
\[
\operatorname{Risk}_{\mathbb P^{\otimes n}}
\left(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}},\Psi(\mathbb P)\right)
\le
C_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right\},
\]
where \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\) is the observed-law optimal-regression value of \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value}.

34be4387b404e536413ad50fe7202c380adb979a.title: Equal-propensity L1 reduction
34be4387b404e536413ad50fe7202c380adb979a.body:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and let \(\epsilon\) be the overlap parameter. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} The sample law \(\mu_n\) is the \(n\)-fold product law generated by an observed law \(\mathbb P_0\), as in \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\).
\item \textbf{(Alphabet size.)} \(2\le d\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap range.)} \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every pair \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), let
\[
\mathbb P=\operatorname{Obs}\{\mathrm{L1Emb}(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\},
\]
where \(\operatorname{Obs}\) is the observed margin from \(\cref{obj:def:observed-margin}\) and \(\mathrm{L1Emb}\) is the embedding in \(\cref{obj:def:l1-embedding}\). The law \(\mathbb P\) belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}\), and, for every \(x\in[d]\),
\[
p_x=\frac{P_x+Q_x}{2}.
\]
Moreover, whenever \(p_x>0\),
\[
\pi_x=\frac12,
\]
and the observed-law optimal-regression value from \(\cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value}\) satisfies
\[
\Psi(\mathbb P)=\frac12+\frac14\sum_{x\in[d]} |P_x-Q_x|.
\]
Finally, the explicit fixed-\(n\) product Markov kernel obtained by applying the single-observation \(L_1\) embedding kernel independently across the \(n\) coordinates transforms the law of \(n\) paired draws from \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\) exactly into the \(n\)-fold product law \(\mathbb P^{\otimes n}\). Consequently, for the fixed-sample minimax squared risk in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\),
\[
\frac{1}{16}\,\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\le \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon},
\]
where \(\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\) denotes the corresponding normalized two-sample \(L_1\) minimax mean-squared risk.

cb81c9f5bb87aaf68eb3a9744d3330fe53dd50fb.title: Simultaneous Jackson certificate
cb81c9f5bb87aaf68eb3a9744d3330fe53dd50fb.body:
There is a universal constant \(A>0\) such that, for every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) with the following property. Let:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(K\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Rectangle.)} \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a valid pilot-local rectangle as in \(\cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}\), with \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge 0\) and positive radii
\[
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}>0
\]
for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(P_{x,K}\) be the tensor Jackson polynomial associated with \(\epsilon\), \(K\), and \(Q_x\) in \(\cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}\). Then the same polynomial satisfies all of the following conclusions:
\[
\deg_{\jmath}(P_{x,K})\le 2(K-1)
\qquad\text{for every }\jmath\in\mathcal J .
\]
For every \(v\in Q_x\),
\[
\left|P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)\right|
\le
C_\epsilon
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left\{
\frac{\sqrt{(v_{\jmath}-\ell_{\jmath,x})(u_{\jmath,x}-v_{\jmath})}}{K}
+
\frac{r_{\jmath,x}}{K^2}
\right\}.
\]
There are a finite multi-index set \(\mathcal A_x\) and coefficients \(b_{x,\alpha}\) such that, for every \(v\),
\[
P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}
b_{x,\alpha}
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left(\frac{v_{\jmath}-b_{\jmath,x}}{r_{\jmath,x}}\right)^{\alpha_{\jmath}},
\]
with
\[
\alpha_{\jmath}\le 2(K-1)
\qquad\text{for every }\alpha\in\mathcal A_x\text{ and every }\jmath\in\mathcal J,
\]
and
\[
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}|b_{x,\alpha}|
\le
A^K(1+\epsilon^{-1})
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x}.
\]

986266ce8d603d9037d21a3f46b3a0d2de9eefa4.title: Centered factorial pilot control
986266ce8d603d9037d21a3f46b3a0d2de9eefa4.body:
Assume the product experiment satisfies the i.i.d. sampling law in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}.  There is a universal Jackson tuning with self-normalized Poisson pilot-radius constant, polynomial-degree constant \(\kappa=1/100000\), and cutoff \(D_0=3\).  For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), there is a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) such that the following assertions hold for every \(n,d\), every observed law \(\mathbb P\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), and every positive sample size \(n\), whenever \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}.  Set \(m=n/8\), let \(q_x=(q_{00,x},q_{01,x},q_{10,x},q_{11,x})\) be the four-coordinate cell vector, and let \(p_x\) be the marginal mass of cell \(x\).

In the uncapped marked experiment generated by
\[
M\sim \operatorname{Pois}(n/4)
\]
together with i.i.d. observations from \(\mathbb P\) and independent fair pilot/evaluation marks, the count \(M\) has law \(\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\).  The induced pilot/evaluation table has law equal to the product, over cells \(x\in[d]\) and coordinates \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), of two independent Poisson count arrays with coordinate means \(m q_{\jmath,x}\).  For each fixed cell \(x\), the marginal law of the pilot and evaluation counts in that cell is therefore
\[
\bigotimes_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\operatorname{Pois}(m q_{\jmath,x})
\otimes
\bigotimes_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\operatorname{Pois}(m q_{\jmath,x}).
\]

For every cell \(x\), every fixed pilot table, every coordinate \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), every \(z\in\mathbb R\), and every \(h,t\in\mathbb N\), conditional expectation over the evaluation counts satisfies
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[U_h(N_{\jmath,x};z)\mid N'\right]
=
(q_{\jmath,x}-z)^h
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[U_h(N_{\jmath,x};z)U_t(N_{\jmath,x};z)\mid N'\right]
=
\sum_{\ell=0}^{\min\{h,t\}}
\binom{h}{\ell}\binom{t}{\ell}\ell!
\left(\frac{q_{\jmath,x}}{m}\right)^\ell
(q_{\jmath,x}-z)^{h+t-2\ell}.
\]

With the same tuning, the clipped Jackson-factorial cell statistic \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\) obeys, uniformly over all cells \(x\in[d]\),
\[
\left|
\mathbb E T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)
\right|
\le
C_\epsilon
\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{p_x}{mL_d}}+\frac{1}{mL_d}
\right\},
\]
\[
\operatorname{Var}(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}})
\le
C_\epsilon d^{1/16}
\left\{
\frac{p_x L_d}{m}+\frac{L_d^2}{m^2}
\right\},
\]
and the pilot-failure contributions satisfy
\[
\mathrm{PF}_{1,x}
\le
C_\epsilon
\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{p_x}{mL_d}}+\frac{1}{mL_d}
\right\},
\qquad
\mathrm{PF}_{2,x}
\le
C_\epsilon d^{1/16}
\left\{
\frac{p_x L_d}{m}+\frac{L_d^2}{m^2}
\right\}.
\]

c99d1efb5f2edc958940c9a645852f891e98debe.title: Global minimax lower bound
c99d1efb5f2edc958940c9a645852f891e98debe.body:
Suppose the observed samples satisfy the independent product sampling law in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}. For every overlap constant \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exists a constant \(c_\epsilon>0\) such that, for every \(n\geq 1\) and \(d\geq 2\), the fixed-sample minimax squared risk \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies
\[
c_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right\}
\leq
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}.
\]

a75780fb60a87f94b1444888719eb004eefd8131.title: Matched minimax frontier
a75780fb60a87f94b1444888719eb004eefd8131.body:
There are universal tuning constants \(H_0>0\), \(0<\kappa<1\), and an integer cutoff \(D_0>2\) for the Jackson factorial estimator such that the following holds.  For every fixed overlap constant \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), there are real constants \(c_\epsilon\) and \(C_\epsilon\) with
\[
0<c_\epsilon\leq C_\epsilon .
\]
For every \(n\geq 1\) and \(d\geq 2\), with \(L_d=\log(ed)\) and with \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) denoting the fixed-sample observed minimax squared risk in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\),
\[
c_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{nL_d}\right\}
\leq
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\leq
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}
E_{\mathbb P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[
  \left(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P)\right)^2
\right]
\leq
C_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{nL_d}\right\}.
\]
Moreover, the fixed-sample minimax squared risk over the full-data causal completion class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) is exactly \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) for the same \(n\), \(d\), and \(\epsilon\).

fb12a536af05f77e505655319ec3e126c95f3f3b.title: Parent minimax reduction
fb12a536af05f77e505655319ec3e126c95f3f3b.body:
There exist tuning constants \(H_0>0\), \(\kappa\in(0,1)\), and an integer cutoff \(D_0>2\), used by the Jackson factorial estimator in \(\cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator}\), such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Matched frontier.)} For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), there are constants \(c\) and \(C\) with \(0<c\leq C\) such that, for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\),
\[
c\min\left\{1,\frac{\sqrt d}{n}+\frac{d}{n\log(en)}\right\}
\leq
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\leq
C\frac{d}{n}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Bounded alphabets.)} For every \(n\), every \(2\leq d<D_0\), every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\), and every observed sample, the Jackson factorial estimator in \(\cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator}\) equals the empirical-ratio estimator in \(\cref{obj:def:empirical-ratio-estimator}\):
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}=\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Bounded-alphabet sequences.)} For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\) and every sequence \(d_n\) with \(d_n\geq2\) for all \(n\) and \(d_n\leq d_{\max}\) for some finite \(d_{\max}\), there are constants \(c\) and \(C\) with \(0<c\leq C\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\frac{c}{n}
\leq
\mathfrak R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}
\leq
\frac{C}{n}.
\]
\end{itemize}

1c5514088806071ac8b1cc7843b618caab9366f0.title: Dense moment matching lower bound
1c5514088806071ac8b1cc7843b618caab9366f0.body:
Suppose the product experiment satisfies the i.i.d. sampling law in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}.  There is an integer cutoff \(D_0\geq2\) such that, for every overlap constant \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), there is a constant \(c_\epsilon>0\) with the following property.  For all integers \(d,n\) satisfying \(d\geq D_0\) and \(d^2<n\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree and amplitude.)} The lower-bound degree and amplitude obey
\[
8L_d\leq K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}<8L_d+2,
\qquad
a_{n,d}^2=\frac{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}d}{128n},
\qquad
a_{n,d}\leq \frac12 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Dense observed submodel.)} For every \(\theta\in[-a_{n,d},a_{n,d}]^d\), the dense equal-mass contrast submodel \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) has observed margin in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and satisfies, for every \(x\in[d]\),
\[
p_x=\frac1d,
\qquad
\pi_x=\frac12,
\qquad
\mu_{1x}=\frac{1+\theta_x}{2},
\qquad
\mu_{0x}=\frac{1-\theta_x}{2},
\]
with
\[
\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
=
\frac12+\frac{1}{2d}\sum_{x=1}^d|\theta_x|.
\]
\item \textbf{(Moment-matched priors and mixtures.)} The two dense product priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\), with induced Poissonized mixtures \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\), may be chosen so that their prior-mean separation satisfies
\[
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}},
\qquad
0<\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}\leq1,
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb M_{0,n,d},\mathbb M_{1,n,d})
\leq
d\{\operatorname{tail}_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}\}^{1/2}
\leq
d\left\{\frac{(e/64)^{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}}{1-e/64}\right\}^{1/2}
\leq\frac1{16}.
\]
Under each of the two product priors, the target is concentrated around its prior mean:
\[
\int
\left(\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
-\mathbb E_{\Pi_{j,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}\right)^2
\,d\Pi_{j,n,d}(\theta)
\leq
\frac{a_{n,d}^2}{4d},
\qquad j\in\{0,1\},
\]
and
\[
\Pi_{j,n,d}\left(
\left|\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
-\mathbb E_{\Pi_{j,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}\right|
>
\frac{\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}}{4}
\right)
\leq
\frac18,
\qquad j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(One-cell likelihood identity.)} For all contrasts \(\theta,\theta'\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E_0[L_\theta L_{\theta'}]
=
\exp(\lambda_{n,d}\theta\theta').
\]
\end{itemize}
Consequently,
\[
c_\epsilon(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}})^2
\leq
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon},
\qquad
c_\epsilon\frac{d}{nK_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}
\leq
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon},
\]
and the fixed-sample and Poissonized risks satisfy
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\geq
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}
-
\Pr\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}.
\]
In particular,
\[
c_\epsilon\frac{d}{nL_d}
\leq
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}.
\]

cd9382ff2af25c973a763adbe2235a3dd861dbac.title: Consistency and parametric boundaries
cd9382ff2af25c973a763adbe2235a3dd861dbac.body:
For every overlap constant \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), and for every alphabet-size sequence \(d_\bullet=(d_n)_{n\ge 1}\) satisfying \(d_n\ge 2\) for all \(n\), the following equivalences hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Observed consistency.)} The fixed-sample minimax squared risk \(\mathfrak R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}\) satisfies
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\longrightarrow 0
\]
if and only if
\[
d_n=o\{n\log(en)\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Causal consistency.)} The causal minimax squared risk over \(\mathcal P_{d_n,\epsilon}\) satisfies
\[
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{causal}}_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\longrightarrow 0
\]
if and only if
\[
d_n=o\{n\log(en)\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Observed parametric boundary.)} The observed minimax risk sequence has the parametric \(n^{-1}\) rate, meaning that there exist constants \(c,C\) with \(0<c\le C\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\frac{c}{n}\le \mathfrak R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\le \frac{C}{n},
\]
if and only if the alphabet-size sequence is uniformly bounded asymptotically, meaning \(d_n=O(1)\).
\item \textbf{(Causal parametric boundary.)} The causal minimax risk sequence has the parametric \(n^{-1}\) rate, meaning that there exist constants \(c,C\) with \(0<c\le C\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\frac{c}{n}\le \mathfrak R^{\mathrm{causal}}_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\le \frac{C}{n},
\]
if and only if \(d_n=O(1)\).
\end{itemize}

ab4d788c88181cbe170aee271d0089581c14637f.title: Identification and completion
ab4d788c88181cbe170aee271d0089581c14637f.body:
Let \(d\ge 2\), let \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), and let \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}. Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Cell overlap.)} For every \(x\in[d]\), the four-vector \(q_x=(q_{00,x},q_{01,x},q_{10,x},q_{11,x})\) belongs to the overlap cone \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\) of \cref{obj:def:overlap-cone}.
\item \textbf{(Observed value.)} The observed-law optimal-regression value of \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value} satisfies
\[
\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_{x=1}^d \bar f_\epsilon(q_x).
\]
\item \textbf{(Global extension bounds.)} For every \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\), the global extension of \cref{obj:def:global-extension} satisfies
\[
0\le \bar f_\epsilon(u)\le s(u).
\]
\item \textbf{(Global Lipschitz property.)} For every \(u,v\in\mathbb R_+^4\),
\[
\left|\bar f_\epsilon(u)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)\right|
\le (1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath}\left|u_{\jmath}-v_{\jmath}\right|.
\]
\item \textbf{(Completion.)} There exists a full-data law \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:model-class} whose observed margin satisfies \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)=\mathbb P\). The completion is consistent and conditionally exchangeable, treatment is independent of the joint potential-outcome vector given \(X\), and the two potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables given \(X\).
\item \textbf{(Observed margins.)} For every full-data law \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), its observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) of \cref{obj:def:observed-margin} belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).
\end{itemize}

5e951827012e04b75cc93fcf3d6a91d07cdcb8db.title: Causal value identification
5e951827012e04b75cc93fcf3d6a91d07cdcb8db.body:
Let \(d\ge 2\), let \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), and let \(P\) be a full-data law satisfying \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\). Then the full-data oracle value in \(\cref{obj:def:oracle-value}\) agrees with the observed-law optimal-regression value in \(\cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value}\) evaluated at the observed margin in \(\cref{obj:def:observed-margin}\):
\[
V^\star(P)=\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P)\}.
\]

4f3fc48891fbbefc7c9aaf408dbddb31ebad6ce2.title: I.i.d. observed sampling
4f3fc48891fbbefc7c9aaf408dbddb31ebad6ce2.body: For each observed law \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), let \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\) denote the observed triple for unit \(i\). The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with common law \(\mathbb P\).

cd08ac7742b56175f3b817164f6570df1ee9c56f.title: Consistency of outcomes
cd08ac7742b56175f3b817164f6570df1ee9c56f.body:
The observed outcome satisfies
\[
Y=Y(A)
\]
almost surely.

b56448aeebb5cfb5f354d3f5019338b45268bd72.title: Conditional exchangeability
b56448aeebb5cfb5f354d3f5019338b45268bd72.body:
For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), the potential outcome \(Y(a)\) is conditionally independent of treatment given covariates:
\[
Y(a)\perp A\mid X .
\]

2c9df75ebcd62ab29b88bf970f47d43eade62d60.title: Fixed overlap
2c9df75ebcd62ab29b88bf970f47d43eade62d60.body:
Let \([d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}\) be the finite covariate alphabet. For every observed law \(\mathbb P\) under consideration and every \(x\in[d]\) with covariate-cell mass \(p_x=\mathbb P(X=x)>0\), the treatment propensity \(\pi_x=\mathbb P(A=1\mid X=x)\) satisfies
\[
\epsilon\leq \pi_x \leq 1-\epsilon ,
\]
where \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\) is the fixed overlap constant.

2351f0c190bffec93274b4482e9c63d96a2e29e0.title: Overlap cone \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\)
2351f0c190bffec93274b4482e9c63d96a2e29e0.body:
The four-cell overlap cone is
\[
\mathcal C_\epsilon
:=
\{u\in\mathbb R_+^4:\epsilon s(u)\leq s_1(u)\leq(1-\epsilon)s(u)\},
\]
where, for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1},
\qquad
s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u).
\]

b6ed0617bf2f2d15ccd46babc860bd0d346da273.title: Global extension \(g_{a,\epsilon}\) and \(\bar f_\epsilon\)
b6ed0617bf2f2d15ccd46babc860bd0d346da273.body:
For \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\) with \(s(u)>0\), define the overlap-stabilized arm contribution
\[
g_{a,\epsilon}(u)
:=
\frac{s(u)u_{a1}}{\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}},
\qquad a\in\{0,1\},
\]
and the globally defined cellwise maximum contribution
\[
\bar f_\epsilon(u)
:=
\max_{a\in\{0,1\}} g_{a,\epsilon}(u).
\]
At the origin,
\[
g_{a,\epsilon}(0)=0,
\qquad
\bar f_\epsilon(0)=0.
\]

401be393f5d537b6f3be1394c2676c7b51b0ec71.title: Oracle value \(V^\star(P)\)
401be393f5d537b6f3be1394c2676c7b51b0ec71.body:
For a full-data law \(P\), the full-data causal optimal-treatment value is
\[
V^\star(P)
=
E_P\!\left[
\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}
E_P\{Y(a)\mid X\}
\right].
\]

f8e381020b8a52cf1b3d3cf84dc49dc98abd7589.title: Empirical-ratio estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\)
f8e381020b8a52cf1b3d3cf84dc49dc98abd7589.body:
For \(x\in[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define the empirical counts
\[
\overline N_x
=
\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{X_i=x\},
\qquad
\overline N_{ax}
=
\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\},
\]
and
\[
\overline S_{ax}
=
\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,Y_i=1\}.
\]
Set
\[
\widehat p_x=\frac{\overline N_x}{n},
\qquad
\widehat\mu_{ax}=\frac{\overline S_{ax}}{\overline N_{ax}},
\]
with the convention \(0/0=0\). The empirical-ratio optimal-value estimator is
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}
=
\sum_{x=1}^d \widehat p_x \max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\widehat\mu_{ax}.
\]

c6815abed3d598650df7e47a48e11be4171f756d.title: Jackson polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\)
c6815abed3d598650df7e47a48e11be4171f756d.body:
For an integer \(K_d\ge 2\), define the order-four Jackson kernel on \([-\pi,\pi]\) by
\[
J_{K_d}(t)
=
c_{K_d}
\left\{
\frac{\sin(K_dt/2)}{\sin(t/2)}
\right\}^{4},
\]
with removable values filled continuously and normalizing constant \(c_{K_d}\) chosen so that
\[
\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} J_{K_d}(t)\,dt=1.
\]
For a rectangle
\[
Q_x
=
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}],
\]
define its coordinate centers and radii by
\[
b_{\jmath,x}
=
\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}
=
\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
The associated tensor polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\) is defined by the even product convolution
\[
P_{x,K_d}(b_x+r_x\odot\cos\theta)
=
\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^4}
\bar f_\epsilon\{b_x+r_x\odot\cos(\theta+t)\}
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}J_{K_d}(t_{\jmath})\,dt.
\]

5db9bb2b5946bfed4aba3c6a201ade3f58ba0b50.title: Jackson-factorial estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\)
5db9bb2b5946bfed4aba3c6a201ade3f58ba0b50.body:
The inputs are \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), the alphabet size \(d\), and tuning constants \(D_0\), \(\kappa\), and \(H_0\).

\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the logarithmic scale, Poissonized scale, and polynomial degree by
\[
L_d=\log(ed),
\qquad
m=\frac n8,
\qquad
K_d=\max\{2,\lfloor \kappa L_d\rfloor\}.
\]

\item If \(d<D_0\), output
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}
=
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}.
\]
If \(d\ge D_0\) and \(n<d/L_d\), output
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}
=
\frac12.
\]

\item In the remaining case, draw
\[
M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4).
\]
On the event \(M>n\), set
\[
\widetilde V=0.
\]

\item On the event \(M\le n\), draw independent marks
\[
B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),
\qquad i=1,\ldots,M.
\]
For each \(x\in[d]\) and coordinate \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), define pilot and evaluation counts
\[
N'_{\jmath,x}
=
\sum_{i=1}^M B_i\,\mathbf 1\{O_i\text{ belongs to coordinate }\jmath\text{ in cell }x\},
\]
and
\[
N_{\jmath,x}
=
\sum_{i=1}^M (1-B_i)\,\mathbf 1\{O_i\text{ belongs to coordinate }\jmath\text{ in cell }x\}.
\]

\item Define pilot frequencies and rectangle half-widths by
\[
c_{\jmath,x}
=
\frac{N'_{\jmath,x}}{m},
\qquad
h_{\jmath,x}
=
H_0
\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{c_{\jmath,x}L_d}{m}}
+
\frac{L_d}{m}
\right\}.
\]
Set
\[
\ell_{\jmath,x}
=
\max\{0,c_{\jmath,x}-h_{\jmath,x}\},
\qquad
u_{\jmath,x}
=
c_{\jmath,x}+h_{\jmath,x},
\]
and
\[
Q_x
=
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}].
\]
Let \(b_x\) and \(r_x\) denote the vector of coordinate centers and coordinate radii of \(Q_x\).

\item Expand the local polynomial as
\[
P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\sum_\alpha
b_{x,\alpha}
\left(\frac{v-b_x}{r_x}\right)^\alpha .
\]
For \(h\ge 0\), define the centered factorial lift
\[
U_h(N;z)
=
\sum_{t=0}^h
\binom ht
(-z)^{h-t}
\frac{(N)_t}{m^t}.
\]

\item Define the clipping scale
\[
S_x
=
(1+\epsilon^{-1})
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x},
\]
the unprojected cell estimate
\[
Z_x
=
\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
+
\sum_\alpha
b_{x,\alpha}
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\frac{
U_{\alpha_{\jmath}}(N_{\jmath,x};b_{\jmath,x})
}{
r_{\jmath,x}^{\alpha_{\jmath}}
},
\]
and the clipped cell estimate
\[
T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}
=
\Pi_{
[\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)-d^{1/4}S_x,\,
 \bar f_\epsilon(b_x)+d^{1/4}S_x]
}
(Z_x).
\]

\item Define the randomized projected aggregate by
\[
\widetilde V
=
\Pi_{[0,1]}
\left(
\sum_{x=1}^d T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}
\right).
\]
The all-data Rao--Blackwellized estimator is
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}
=
E\!\left[
\widetilde V
\mid
O_1,\ldots,O_n
\right],
\]
where the conditional expectation integrates only the auxiliary Poisson count \(M\) and marks \(B_1,\ldots,B_M\).
\end{enumerate}

494779e8883eb0720793b52e57cc03b01977f457.title: \(L_1\) embedding \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\)
494779e8883eb0720793b52e57cc03b01977f457.body:
For \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), define the observed atom masses
\[
q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=\frac{P_x}{4},
\qquad
q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=\frac{Q_x}{4},
\qquad x\in[d].
\]
Complete the observed law by taking the potential outcomes to be conditionally independent Bernoulli variables, setting the treatment propensity equal to \(1/2\), and imposing consistency.

a877a00b58f7c1560f4af5c9fee3ac469b1cfa31.title: Observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\)
a877a00b58f7c1560f4af5c9fee3ac469b1cfa31.body:
For a full-data law \(P\), its observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) is the law on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) defined by
\[
\operatorname{Obs}(P)\{(x,a,y)\}
=
P(X=x,A=a,Y=y),
\qquad
(x,a,y)\in[d]\times\{0,1\}^2.
\]

918514435569fe2d892fb0e94bb97e7d2499e160.title: Observed-law class \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\)
918514435569fe2d892fb0e94bb97e7d2499e160.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:ass:fixed-overlap}\), let
\[
\Delta_d=\left\{p\in[0,1]^d:\sum_{x=1}^d p_x=1\right\}.
\]
The class \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) consists of all laws \(\mathbb P\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) for which there exist \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)\in\Delta_d\), propensities \(\pi_x\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), and means \(\mu_{ax}\in[0,1]\) such that, for every \(x\in[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
q_{a1,x}
=
p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}\mu_{ax},
\qquad
q_{a0,x}
=
p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}(1-\mu_{ax}),
\]
where
\[
q_{ay,x}=\mathbb P(X=x,A=a,Y=y).
\]
For each cell \(x\), write
\[
q_x=(q_{00,x},q_{01,x},q_{10,x},q_{11,x}).
\]
The support contains at most \(d\) covariate cells, and on any null cell the parameters may be chosen arbitrarily within the displayed ranges.

e1d84257dd168b3d80e26eb9c5e2bfb46e6526dc.title: Observed-law optimal value \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\)
e1d84257dd168b3d80e26eb9c5e2bfb46e6526dc.body:
For \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}\), with table \(\mathbf q=(q_x)_{x=1}^d\), the observed-law optimal-regression functional is
\[
\Psi(\mathbb P)=\Psi(\mathbf q)
:=
\sum_{x=1}^d p_x\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\mu_{ax}.
\]
This value is independent of the permitted choice of \(\mu_{ax}\) on cells with \(p_x=0\).

c19d13e9a67b0ad183ff1796ad03f2f9c69a8e24.title: Minimax risk \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\)
c19d13e9a67b0ad183ff1796ad03f2f9c69a8e24.body:
The fixed-sample minimax squared risk is
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
:=
\inf_{\widehat V}
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}
E_{\mathbb P}
\left[
\left\{
\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\Psi(\mathbb P)
\right\}^2
\right],
\]
where the infimum is over all measurable maps
\[
\widehat V:\bigl([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\bigr)^n\to\mathbb R.
\]

85adc756bff9cde9deb5e59a99cec4ee5912e2d0.title: Dense construction \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\)
85adc756bff9cde9deb5e59a99cec4ee5912e2d0.body:
For \(\theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\), define \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) by
\[
p_x=\frac1d,\qquad
\pi_x=\frac12,\qquad
\mu_{1x}=\frac{1+\theta_x}{2},\qquad
\mu_{0x}=\frac{1-\theta_x}{2}.
\]
Complete the observed law by drawing \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, drawing \(A\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of the potential outcomes, and setting
\[
Y=Y(A).
\]
For even \(K\), define
\[
E_K
=
\inf_{p:\deg(p)\le K}
\sup_{t\in[-1,1]}
\bigl||t|-p(t)\bigr|.
\]
Let \(\nu_{0,K}\) and \(\nu_{1,K}\) be the symmetric probability measures obtained from the negative and positive parts of twice a symmetrized norm-one Hahn--Banach measure that annihilates every polynomial of degree at most \(K\) and integrates \(|t|\) to \(E_K\). Their moments agree through degree \(K\), and
\[
\int |t|\,d\nu_{1,K}(t)
-
\int |t|\,d\nu_{0,K}(t)
=
2E_K.
\]
Set
\[
K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil 4L_d\rceil,\qquad
\lambda_{n,d}=\frac{2n}{d},\qquad
a_{n,d}=\sqrt{\frac{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}{64\lambda_{n,d}}}.
\]
Let \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) be the pushforward of \(\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) under the coordinatewise scaling map \(t\mapsto a_{n,d}t\), and let \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\) be the analogous pushforward of \(\nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\). Let \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) be the corresponding observation mixtures when the total sample size is independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\).

In the Poissonized experiment, define
\[
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}
:=
\inf_{\widehat V}
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}
E_{\mathbb P}
\left[
\left\{
\widehat V-\Psi(\mathbb P)
\right\}^2
\right],
\]
and define the dense prior-mean separation by
\[
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
:=
E_{\Pi_{1,n,d}}
\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
-
E_{\Pi_{0,n,d}}
\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}.
\]

e26093ae71f53425c6520107a4b03d0564e3cc88.title: Constant route \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\)
e26093ae71f53425c6520107a4b03d0564e3cc88.body: The route \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\) rescales the pilot-local four-cell rectangles by their Poisson noise geometry, optimizes the tensor-polynomial bias--variance functional for \(\bar f_\epsilon\), and dualizes the approximation constraint into moment-matched observed laws in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) for the target \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\).

b0c36c727b8e2c0aa808b831c55759f973c49e51.title: Sharp overlap constant
b0c36c727b8e2c0aa808b831c55759f973c49e51.body:
A natural next question is whether, along each nonsaturated sequence with \(d\to\infty\) and
\[
\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\to0,
\]
the normalized risk
\[
\frac{n\log(ed)}{d}\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\]
converges to a finite positive limit, and whether an estimator attaining that limit can be derived through \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\).

36d7835a39fd5510baa9b2bd4cfe25ddb2cb69ff.title: Full-data causal class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\)

c121dc768cbedac555971eabb6dfe56ac6377957.title: Jackson factorial upper bound
c121dc768cbedac555971eabb6dfe56ac6377957.body:
Assume the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} For every finite observed law and every sample size, the sample law is the canonical i.i.d. product law of \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}.
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap constant satisfies \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Sizes.)} The sample size and alphabet size satisfy \(n\ge 1\) and \(d\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} The observed law \(\mathbb P\) belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}.
\end{itemize}
Then there exist universal tuning constants \(H_0>0\), \(\kappa\in(0,1)\), and an integer cutoff \(D_0>2\) such that the estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator} has the following property: for every overlap constant \(\epsilon\) satisfying the overlap condition, there is a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) such that, for every \(n,d,\mathbb P\) satisfying the size and model-class conditions,
\[
\operatorname{Risk}_{\mathbb P^{\otimes n}}
\left(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}},\Psi(\mathbb P)\right)
\le
C_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right\}.
\]
Here \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\) is the observed-law optimal-regression value of \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value}.

e3f0e3ed62a3ce9c923abc9c97895741d78e4ad8.title: Dense matching construction
e3f0e3ed62a3ce9c923abc9c97895741d78e4ad8.body:
For \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), a domain certificate
\[
2\le d,\qquad
0<\epsilon<\frac12,\qquad
0<a_{n,d}\le \frac12,
\]
where
\[
K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil 4L_d\rceil,\qquad
\lambda_{n,d}=\frac{2n}{d},\qquad
a_{n,d}=\sqrt{\frac{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}{64\lambda_{n,d}}},
\]
and a supplied dense prior family \(K\mapsto(\nu_{0,K},\nu_{1,K})\) with its moment-matching certificates at every positive even degree, the dense moment-matching construction is the object with components
\[
P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}},\qquad
E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}},\qquad
K_d^{\mathrm{lb}},\qquad
\lambda_{n,d},\qquad
a_{n,d},
\]
where \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) is the potential-outcome law induced by the dense full-data cell masses, and
\[
E_K
=
\inf\left\{\ne\in\mathbb R:
\exists p,\ \deg(p)\le K\ \text{and}\ 
\sup_{t\in[-1,1]}\bigl||t|-p(t)\bigr|\le e
\right\}.
\]
At degree \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\), the coordinate priors are
\[
\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}},\qquad
\nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}},
\]
the dense product priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\) are obtained by restricting the corresponding product measures to \([-1,1]^d\), scaling each coordinate by \(a_{n,d}\), and mapping into the dense contrast class, and the observation mixtures are
\[
\mathbb M_{0,n,d}
=
\operatorname{Obs}_{n,d}\circ \Pi_{0,n,d},
\qquad
\mathbb M_{1,n,d}
=
\operatorname{Obs}_{n,d}\circ \Pi_{1,n,d},
\]
where the observation kernel uses an independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\) sample. The associated Poissonized risk component is
\[
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon},
\]
and the prior target-mean separation component is
\[
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
E_{\Pi_{1,n,d}}
\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
-
E_{\Pi_{0,n,d}}
\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}.
\]
The construction also carries the supplied prior-pair certificate at degree \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\) and the identities
\[
K=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}},
\qquad
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}.
\]

40f5ae351e59357c50afb754fba2c14d8ca446f5.title: Jackson factorial risk bound
40f5ae351e59357c50afb754fba2c14d8ca446f5.body:
Assume the sampling condition of \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}: for every alphabet size \(d\), sample size \(n\), and observed finite law \(\mathbb P\), the sample law is the canonical i.i.d. product law generated by \(\mathbb P\).

Then there exist tuning constants \(H_0>0\), \(\kappa\in(0,1)\), and an integer cutoff \(D_0>2\) such that the Jackson factorial estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator} satisfies the following bound. For every overlap constant \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge 1\), every \(d\ge 2\), and every observed law \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class},
\[
\operatorname{Risk}_{\mathbb P}
\left(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}},\Psi(\mathbb P)\right)
\le
C_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right\}.
\]
Here \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\) is the observed-law optimal-regression value of \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value}.

8f0a547c745b5abebdbd9778d95923e00a48fc1f.title: Dense moment matching
8f0a547c745b5abebdbd9778d95923e00a48fc1f.body:
For \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), a dense domain certificate
\[
2\le d,\qquad
0<\epsilon,\qquad
\epsilon<\frac12,\qquad
0<a_{n,d}\le \frac12,
\]
and a dense prior family \(K\mapsto(\nu_{0,K},\nu_{1,K})\) with its moment-matching certificate at every positive even degree \(K\), the dense moment-matching construction is the object with the following components:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dense law.)} For each \(\theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\), \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) is the potential-outcome probability law induced by the dense full-data cell masses.
\item \textbf{(Approximation scale.)}
\[
K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil 4L_d\rceil,\qquad
E_K=\inf\left\{e\in\mathbb R:\exists p,\ \deg(p)\le K\ \text{and}\ 
\forall t\in[-1,1],\ \bigl||t|-p(t)\bigr|\le e\right\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Poisson intensity and amplitude.)}
\[
\lambda_{n,d}=\frac{2n}{d},\qquad
a_{n,d}=\sqrt{\frac{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}{64\lambda_{n,d}}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Coordinate priors.)} The two coordinate priors are
\[
\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}},\qquad \nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Dense product priors.)} The priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\) are obtained by restricting the product measures \(\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) and \(\nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) to \([-1,1]^d\), scaling each coordinate by \(a_{n,d}\), and mapping the result into the dense contrast class.
\item \textbf{(Observation mixtures.)} The mixtures \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) are the observation-kernel mixtures induced by \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\), with independent Poissonized sample size \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\).
\item \textbf{(Risk and separation.)} The risk component is \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}\), and the prior target-mean separation component is
\[
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
\operatorname{DenseMean}_{n,d,\epsilon}(\nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}})
-
\operatorname{DenseMean}_{n,d,\epsilon}(\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}).
\]
\end{itemize}
The construction also carries the supplied prior-pair certificate at degree \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\) and the identities
\[
K=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}},\qquad
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}.
\]

a1d2a9fb91cdd026459710c9d66a73215b91c49a.title: Jackson factorial risk bound
a1d2a9fb91cdd026459710c9d66a73215b91c49a.body:
Assume the sampling condition in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}: for every alphabet size \(d\), sample size \(n\), and observed finite law \(\mathbb P\), the sample law is the canonical i.i.d. product law generated by \(\mathbb P\).

Then there exist tuning constants \(H_0>0\), \(\kappa\in(0,1)\), and an integer cutoff \(D_0>2\) such that the Jackson factorial estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator} satisfies the following guarantee whenever:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap constant \(\epsilon\) satisfies \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} The sample size satisfies \(n\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Alphabet size.)} The alphabet size satisfies \(d\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Observed model.)} The observed law \(\mathbb P\) belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}.
\end{itemize}
For every such \(\epsilon\), there is a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) such that, for every such \(n,d\), and \(\mathbb P\),
\[
\operatorname{Risk}_{\mathbb P}
\left(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}},\Psi\right)
\le
C_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right\}.
\]
Here \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\) is the observed-law optimal-regression value of \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value}.

c909e0bfe0e46b12997aa3ffc3c699421f10793f.title: Dense amplitude range
c909e0bfe0e46b12997aa3ffc3c699421f10793f.body:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(2\le d\) and \(d^2<n\). For the lower-bound contrast amplitude \(a_{n,d}\) defined in \cref{obj:def:dense-moment-matching-construction},
\[
0<a_{n,d}\le \frac12.
\]

83c0e5c25a19c2d566fc1e515fcce32956e3b3b2.title: Bad pilot moment bound
83c0e5c25a19c2d566fc1e515fcce32956e3b3b2.body:
Fix the four-coordinate set \(\mathcal J=\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\). Let \(q=(q_\jmath)_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\) have nonnegative coordinates, let \(m>0\), let \(L\ge 1\), and let \(t\in\{1,2,4\}\). Suppose the pilot counts \((N'_{\jmath})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\) are independent with
\[
N'_{\jmath}\sim \operatorname{Pois}(m q_\jmath),
\qquad \jmath\in\mathcal J .
\]
With \(H_0=1024\), define the normalized aggregate pilot score
\[
\Gamma(N')
=
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left[
\left|{N'_{\jmath}\over m}-q_\jmath\right|
+

d280092331ade200f55fdb072fa84ab07253f73f.title: Normalized coefficient envelope
d280092331ade200f55fdb072fa84ab07253f73f.body:
Let \(\epsilon>0\), let \(K\ge2\) be an integer, and let
\[
Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]
\]
be a four-coordinate rectangle satisfying the validity restrictions in \(\cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative lower endpoints.)} For every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive radii.)} With
\[
b_{\jmath,x}=\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\]
one has \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(P_{x,K}\) be the Jackson tensor polynomial from \(\cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}\), and write the centered normalized expansion
\[
P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}
b_{x,\alpha}\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left(\frac{v_\jmath-b_{\jmath,x}}{r_{\jmath,x}}\right)^{\alpha_\jmath},
\]
where \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is the globally defined cellwise maximum contribution in \(\cref{obj:def:global-extension}\). Then
\[

1ef002284c49a173042568c1b611fe588cbf5853.title: Tensor Jackson modulus
1ef002284c49a173042568c1b611fe588cbf5853.body:
Let \(D\) be a nonnegative integer, let \(K\) be a positive integer, and let \(J_K\) be the order-four Jackson kernel from \(\cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}\).  Let \(f:\mathbb R^{D}\to\mathbb R\), let \(L\in\mathbb R\), let \(a_i,b_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(i=1,\ldots,D\), and fix an angle vector \(\varphi\in\mathbb R^{D}\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Scale.)} \(L\ge0\).
\item \textbf{(Continuity.)} The function \(f\) is continuous on the normalized cube \([-1,1]^D\).
\item \textbf{(Weights.)} \(a_i\ge0\) and \(b_i\ge0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,D\).
\item \textbf{(Weighted increment bound.)} For every shift \(\tau\in\mathbb R^{D}\),
\[
\left|f\{\cos(\varphi-\tau)\}-f(\cos\varphi)\right|
\le
L\sum_{i=1}^{D}\left(a_i|\tau_i|+b_i\tau_i^2\right),
\]
where cosine is applied coordinatewise.
\end{itemize}
Define the order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution by
\[
(\mathcal J_K f)(\varphi)
=
\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^D}
f\{\cos(\varphi-\tau)\}
\prod_{i=1}^{D} J_K(\tau_i)\,d\tau .
\]
Then
\[
\left|(\mathcal J_K f)(\varphi)-f(\cos\varphi)\right|
\le
L\sum_{i=1}^{D}
\left\{\frac{32a_i}{K}+\frac{64b_i}{K^2}\right\}.
\]

699c03c59856cd8e08f11764096444b9e04dbfe8.title: Good-pilot aggregate radius
699c03c59856cd8e08f11764096444b9e04dbfe8.body:
Fix \(m>0\), an integer \(d\ge 1\), and let \(L_d=\log(ed)\), the logarithmic alphabet scale. For the four-coordinate set \(\mathcal J=\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), let \(N'_{\jmath,x}\in\mathbb N\) be arbitrary pilot counts and let \(q_\jmath\in\mathbb R\), \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative intensities.)} \(q_\jmath\ge 0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Canonical pilot rectangle.)} With \(c_{\jmath,x}=N'_{\jmath,x}/m\) and the canonical pilot half-width \(h_{\jmath,x}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator}\), define
\[
\ell_{\jmath,x}=\max\{0,c_{\jmath,x}-h_{\jmath,x}\},\qquad
u_{\jmath,x}=c_{\jmath,x}+h_{\jmath,x},\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Good pilot.)} The pilot counts satisfy
\[
|c_{\jmath,x}-q_\jmath|\le \frac{h_{\jmath,x}}{4}
\qquad\text{for every }\jmath\in\mathcal J.
\]
\end{itemize}
Writing \(p_x=\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}q_\jmath\), the aggregate radius obeys
\[
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x}
\le
2\cdot 10^{6}
\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{p_x L_d}{m}}+\frac{L_d}{m}
\right\}.
\]

8609abfbb7155a8f32ca9358dd9ecc036b3cd02d.title: Jackson tensor extraction
8609abfbb7155a8f32ca9358dd9ecc036b3cd02d.body:
Let \(\epsilon>0\), let \(K\ge 2\) be an integer, and let
\(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a four-coordinate rectangle.  For each \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), write
\[
b_{\jmath,x}=\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative lower endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge 0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Positive radii.)} \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist a polynomial \(P_{x,K}\) in the four physical coordinates and a polynomial \(\mathcal R_{x,K}\) in the four normalized coordinates such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Physical degree.)} Every coordinate degree of \(P_{x,K}\) is at most \(2(K-1)\).
\item \textbf{(Normalized degree.)} Every multi-index \(\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})\) satisfies \(\beta_\omega\le 2(K-1)\) for every normalized coordinate \(\omega\).
\item \textbf{(Centered evaluation.)} For every \(v:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\mathcal R_{x,K}\left(\left\{\frac{v_\jmath-b_{\jmath,x}}{r_{\jmath,x}}\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right),
\]
where \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is the global cellwise maximum contribution from \(\cref{obj:def:global-extension}\).
\item \textbf{(Tensor convolution evaluation.)} For every angle vector \(\vartheta:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
P_{x,K}\left(\left\{b_{\jmath,x}+r_{\jmath,x}\cos(\vartheta_\jmath)\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right)
=
\mathsf J_{\epsilon,K,Q_x}(\vartheta),
\]
where \(\mathsf J_{\epsilon,K,Q_x}\) is the order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution for \(Q_x\) specified in \(\cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}\).
\item \textbf{(Coefficient envelope.)} The normalized coefficient one-norm obeys
\[
\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})}|(\mathcal R_{x,K})_\beta|
\le
2^{40K+20}(1+\epsilon^{-1})
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x}.
\]
\end{itemize}

3ac3e5675f9d8097eaeb0eec2f2c90e16fbccf0e.title: Equal-propensity L1 reduction
3ac3e5675f9d8097eaeb0eec2f2c90e16fbccf0e.body:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and let \(\epsilon\) be the overlap parameter. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} The sample law \(\mu_n\) is the \(n\)-fold product law generated by an observed law \(\mathbb P_0\), as in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}.
\item \textbf{(Alphabet size.)} \(2\le d\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap range.)} \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every pair \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), let
\[
\mathbb P=\operatorname{Obs}\{\mathrm{L1Emb}(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\},
\]
where \(\operatorname{Obs}\) is the observed margin from \cref{obj:def:observed-margin} and \(\mathrm{L1Emb}\) is the embedding in \cref{obj:synth_6}. The law \(\mathbb P\) belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}, and, for every \(x\in[d]\),
\[
p_x=\frac{P_x+Q_x}{2}.
\]
Moreover, whenever \(p_x>0\),
\[
\pi_x=\frac12,
\]
and the observed-law optimal-regression value from \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value} satisfies
\[
\Psi(\mathbb P)=\frac12+\frac14\sum_{x\in[d]} |P_x-Q_x|.
\]
Finally, the explicit fixed-\(n\) product Markov kernel obtained by applying the single-observation \(L_1\) embedding kernel independently across the \(n\) coordinates transforms the law of \(n\) paired draws from \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\) exactly into the \(n\)-fold product law \(\mathbb P^{\otimes n}\). Consequently, for the fixed-sample minimax squared risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk},
\[
\frac{1}{16}\,\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\le \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon},
\]
where \(\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\) is the corresponding normalized two-sample \(L_1\) minimax mean-squared risk.

c7d7c65198d93689aa0d1423eb91487efb8bdf44.title: Dense matching construction
c7d7c65198d93689aa0d1423eb91487efb8bdf44.body:
For \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), a dense domain certificate
\[
2\le d,\qquad
0<\epsilon,\qquad
\epsilon<\frac12,\qquad
0<a_{n,d},\qquad
a_{n,d}\le \frac12,
\]
and a dense prior family \(K\mapsto(\nu_{0,K},\nu_{1,K})\) with its dense prior-pair certificate at every positive even degree \(K\), the dense moment-matching construction is the following object:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dense law.)} For each dense contrast \(\theta\), \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) is the potential-outcome law induced by the dense full-data masses.
\item \textbf{(Approximation error and degree.)} The approximation error is
\[
E_K=\inf\left\{e\in\mathbb R:\exists p\in\mathbb R[t]\ \text{with}\ \deg(p)\le K\ \text{and}\ 
\forall t\in[-1,1],\ \bigl||t|-p(t)\bigr|\le e\right\},
\]
evaluated at
\[
K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil4L_d\rceil .
\]
\item \textbf{(Poisson intensity and amplitude.)} The intensity and amplitude are
\[
\lambda_{n,d}=\frac{2n}{d},\qquad
a_{n,d}=\sqrt{\frac{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}{64\lambda_{n,d}}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Coordinate priors.)} The two coordinate priors are
\[
\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}},\qquad \nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}},
\]
where \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\) is viewed as the positive even degree certified by \(2\le d\).
\item \textbf{(Dense product priors.)} The priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\) are the pushforwards of the restrictions of \(\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) and \(\nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) to \([-1,1]^d\) under the map that sends \(t\) to the dense contrast with coordinates \(a_{n,d}t_x\).
\item \textbf{(Observation mixtures.)} The mixtures \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) are the observation-kernel mixtures induced by \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\), respectively, with Poisson cell intensity \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\).
\item \textbf{(Risk and separation.)} The Poissonized risk component is \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}\). The prior target-mean separation component is
\[
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
E_{\Pi_{1,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
-
E_{\Pi_{0,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}.
\]
\end{itemize}
The construction also carries the supplied prior-pair certificate at degree \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\) and the identities
\[
K=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}},\qquad
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}.
\]

1720299fb38da9b63b367bbb50c41698ed0287bc.title: Dense contrast law
1720299fb38da9b63b367bbb50c41698ed0287bc.body:
For an integer \(d\geq 2\) and a contrast vector \(\theta=(\theta_x)_{x\in[d]}\) with \(\theta_x\in[-1/2,1/2]\) for every \(x\in[d]\), define \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) as the full-data probability law on \((X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\) whose atom at \((x,a,y,y_0,y_1)\in[d]\times\{0,1\}^4\) is
\[
P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}(x,a,y,y_0,y_1)
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{1}{2d}\, b_{(1-\theta_x)/2}(y_0)\, b_{(1+\theta_x)/2}(y_1),
& y=y_a,\\[0.8em]
0,
& y\neq y_a,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(y_a=y_1\) if \(a=1\) and \(y_a=y_0\) if \(a=0\), and \(b_\mu(1)=\mu\), \(b_\mu(0)=1-\mu\).

5b73e915e2501d42f6013a5b82f82668eb891db9.title: Treatment-outcome coordinate set
5b73e915e2501d42f6013a5b82f82668eb891db9.body:
The treatment-outcome coordinate set \(\mathcal J\) is
\[
\mathcal J:=\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}.
\]
A coordinate index is denoted by \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).

af8b1f9e84b6908e52fb3ecc9f8f4cf6c68a5adf.title: Equal-propensity \(L_1\) reduction
af8b1f9e84b6908e52fb3ecc9f8f4cf6c68a5adf.body:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), let \(\epsilon\) be the overlap parameter, let \(\mathbb P_0\) be an observed law on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), and let \(\mu_n\) be a law for \(n\) observed triples. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} The sample law \(\mu_n\) is the \(n\)-fold product law generated by \(\mathbb P_0\), as in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}.
\item \textbf{(Alphabet size.)} \(2\le d\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap range.)} \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every pair \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), let
\[
\mathbb P=\operatorname{Obs}\{\mathrm{L1Emb}(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\},
\]
where \(\operatorname{Obs}\) is the observed margin from \cref{obj:def:observed-margin} and \(\mathrm{L1Emb}\) is the embedding in \cref{obj:synth_6}. The law \(\mathbb P\) belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}, and, for every \(x\in[d]\),
\[
p_x=\frac{P_x+Q_x}{2}.
\]
Moreover, whenever \(p_x>0\),
\[
\pi_x=\frac12,
\]
and the observed-law optimal-regression value from \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value} satisfies
\[
\Psi(\mathbb P)=\frac12+\frac14\sum_{x\in[d]} |P_x-Q_x|.
\]
Finally, the explicit fixed-\(n\) product Markov kernel that applies the single-observation \(L_1\) embedding kernel independently across the \(n\) coordinates sends the law of \(n\) paired draws from \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\) exactly to the \(n\)-fold product law generated by \(\mathbb P\). Consequently, for the fixed-sample minimax squared risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk},
\[
\frac{1}{16}\,\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\le \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon},
\]
where \(\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\) is the corresponding normalized two-sample \(L_1\) minimax mean-squared risk.

2b30378c1a5ff1d291dab3366b7151fcb85bb993.title: Jackson tensor extraction
2b30378c1a5ff1d291dab3366b7151fcb85bb993.body:
Let \(\epsilon\) be the overlap parameter, let \(K\) be an integer approximation degree, and let
\(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a four-coordinate rectangle.  For each \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), write
\[
b_{\jmath,x}=\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive overlap parameter.)} \(\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Approximation degree.)} \(K\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative lower endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge 0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Positive radii.)} \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist a polynomial \(P_{x,K}\) in the four physical coordinates and a polynomial \(\mathcal R_{x,K}\) in the four normalized coordinates such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Physical degree.)} Every coordinate degree of \(P_{x,K}\) is at most \(2(K-1)\).
\item \textbf{(Normalized degree.)} Every multi-index \(\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})\) satisfies \(\beta_\omega\le 2(K-1)\) for every normalized coordinate \(\omega\).
\item \textbf{(Centered evaluation.)} For every \(v:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\mathcal R_{x,K}\left(\left\{\frac{v_\jmath-b_{\jmath,x}}{r_{\jmath,x}}\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right),
\]
where \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is the global cellwise maximum contribution from \cref{obj:def:global-extension}.
\item \textbf{(Tensor convolution evaluation.)} For every angle vector \(\vartheta:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
P_{x,K}\left(\left\{b_{\jmath,x}+r_{\jmath,x}\cos(\vartheta_\jmath)\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right)
=
\mathsf J_{\epsilon,K,Q_x}(\vartheta),
\]
where \(\mathsf J_{\epsilon,K,Q_x}\) is the order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution associated with \(Q_x\) in \cref{obj:synth_17}.
\item \textbf{(Coefficient envelope.)} The normalized coefficient one-norm obeys
\[
\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})}|(\mathcal R_{x,K})_\beta|
\le
2^{40K+20}(1+\epsilon^{-1})
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x}.
\]
\end{itemize}

591d680db58c00d35f8c12f7f5a845de2af6cd8a.title: Tensor polynomial extraction
591d680db58c00d35f8c12f7f5a845de2af6cd8a.body:
Let \(\mathcal J\) be the four outcome-arm coordinate set used in \cref{obj:ass:fixed-overlap}. Let \(\epsilon\) be a positive overlap parameter, let \(K\) be an integer approximation degree, and let
\(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a four-coordinate rectangle as in \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}. For each \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), write
\[
b_{\jmath,x}=\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Approximation degree.)} \(K\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative lower endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge 0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Positive overlap parameter.)} \(\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive radii.)} \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist a polynomial \(P_{x,K}\) in the four physical coordinates and a polynomial \(\mathcal R_{x,K}\) in the four normalized coordinates such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Physical degree.)} Every coordinate degree of \(P_{x,K}\) is at most \(2(K-1)\).
\item \textbf{(Normalized degree.)} Every multi-index \(\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})\) satisfies \(\beta_\omega\le 2(K-1)\) for every normalized coordinate \(\omega\).
\item \textbf{(Centered evaluation.)} For every \(v:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\mathcal R_{x,K}\left(\left\{\frac{v_\jmath-b_{\jmath,x}}{r_{\jmath,x}}\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right),
\]
where \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is the global cellwise maximum contribution from \cref{obj:def:global-extension}.
\item \textbf{(Tensor convolution evaluation.)} For every angle vector \(\vartheta:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
P_{x,K}\left(\left\{b_{\jmath,x}+r_{\jmath,x}\cos(\vartheta_\jmath)\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right)
=
\mathsf J_{\epsilon,K,Q_x}(\vartheta),
\]
where \(\mathsf J_{\epsilon,K,Q_x}\) is the order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution of \(\bar f_\epsilon\) precomposed with the affine parametrization of \(Q_x\), as in \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}.
\item \textbf{(Coefficient envelope.)} The normalized coefficient one-norm obeys
\[
\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})}|(\mathcal R_{x,K})_\beta|
\le
2^{40K+20}(1+\epsilon^{-1})
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x}.
\]
\end{itemize}

61cf25fdaa06927517bf300025dfe3d14071da43.title: Tensor convolution modulus
61cf25fdaa06927517bf300025dfe3d14071da43.body:
Let \(D\) be a finite coordinate dimension and let \(K\) be a positive integer. Let \(f:\mathbb R^D\to\mathbb R\), let \(L\ge0\), let \(a_i\ge0\) and \(b_i\ge0\) for each \(i\in[D]\), and fix \(\varphi\in\mathbb R^D\). Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Kernel.)} The order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution is formed from the order-four Jackson kernel in \(\cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}\).
\item \textbf{(Continuity.)} The function \(f\) is continuous on the normalized cube \([-1,1]^D\).
\item \textbf{(Weighted increment modulus.)} For every shift \(\tau\in\mathbb R^D\),
\[
\left|f\{\cos(\varphi-\tau)\}-f(\cos\varphi)\right|
\le
L\sum_{i=1}^D\left(a_i|\tau_i|+b_i\tau_i^2\right),
\]
where cosine is applied coordinatewise.
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\left|(\mathcal J_K f)(\varphi)-f(\cos\varphi)\right|
\le
L\sum_{i=1}^D\left(\frac{32a_i}{K}+\frac{64b_i}{K^2}\right).
\]

e105b8c0bc93e6f1290dd3ff6789c76f85c091cb.title: Jackson tensor extraction
e105b8c0bc93e6f1290dd3ff6789c76f85c091cb.body:
Let \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), let \(K\) be an integer, and let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a four-coordinate rectangle with center coordinates
\[
b_{\jmath,x}=\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2}
\]
and radii
\[
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(K\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Lower endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge 0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap parameter.)} \(\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Radii.)} \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist a polynomial \(P_{x,K}\) in the four physical coordinates and a polynomial \(\mathcal R_{x,K}\) in the four normalized coordinates such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Physical degree.)} Every coordinate degree of \(P_{x,K}\) is at most \(2(K-1)\).
\item \textbf{(Normalized degree.)} Every \(\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})\) satisfies \(\beta_\omega\le 2(K-1)\) for each coordinate \(\omega\).
\item \textbf{(Centered evaluation.)} For every four-coordinate vector \(v\),
\[
P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\mathcal R_{x,K}\left(\left\{\frac{v_\jmath-b_{\jmath,x}}{r_{\jmath,x}}\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right).
\]
\item \textbf{(Jackson convolution.)} For every angle vector \(\vartheta:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
P_{x,K}\left(\left\{b_{\jmath,x}+r_{\jmath,x}\cos(\vartheta_\jmath)\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right)
\]
equals the order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution of \(\bar f_\epsilon\) precomposed with the affine parametrization of \(Q_x\), evaluated at \(\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Coefficient envelope.)}
\[
\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})}\left|(\mathcal R_{x,K})_\beta\right|
\le
2^{40K+20}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}.
\]
\end{itemize}

f0b42748d6aec8fd265b29722aecebe2414a3fd8.title: Good pilot radius bound
f0b42748d6aec8fd265b29722aecebe2414a3fd8.body:
Fix \(m>0\), an integer \(d\ge 1\), pilot counts \(N'_{\jmath,x}\) for \(\jmath\) in the four-coordinate set \(\mathcal J\), and coordinate intensities \(q_\jmath\ge 0\).  Let \(L_d=\log(ed)\), set \(p_x=\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}q_\jmath\), and let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be the canonical pilot rectangle of \(\cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator}\), with radii
\[
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
Assume that the good-pilot event
\[
\mathsf G_x=\bigcap_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left\{\left|c_{\jmath,x}-q_\jmath\right|\le \frac{h_{\jmath,x}}{4}\right\},
\qquad c_{\jmath,x}=\frac{N'_{\jmath,x}}{m},
\]
holds, where \(h_{\jmath,x}\) is the canonical pilot half-width in \(\cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator}\).  Then
\[
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x}
\le
2\cdot 10^6
\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{p_x L_d}{m}}+\frac{L_d}{m}
\right\}.
\]

bd208d83815dde523202d64bb2033645b8ad9b81.title: Normalized coefficient envelope
bd208d83815dde523202d64bb2033645b8ad9b81.body:
Let \(\epsilon>0\), let \(K\ge2\) be an integer, and let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a four-coordinate rectangle from \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Validity.)} \(Q_x\) is valid in the sense of \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}.
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative lower endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Positive radii.)} With
\[
b_{\jmath,x}=\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\]
one has \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(b_x=(b_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\), \(r_x=(r_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\), and let \(P_{x,K}\) be the Jackson tensor polynomial attached to \(Q_x\). Define the centered normalized polynomial
\[
\mathcal R_{x,K}(z)
=
P_{x,K}(b_x+r_x\odot z)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x} b_{x,\alpha}\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} z_\jmath^{\alpha_\jmath},
\]
where \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is the global cell extension from \cref{obj:def:global-extension} and \(\mathcal A_x=\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})\). Then
\[
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}|b_{x,\alpha}|
\le
(2^{60})^{K}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}.
\]
Moreover, every \(\alpha\in\mathcal A_x\) satisfies
\[
\alpha_\jmath\le 2(K-1)
\]
for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).

244def8ad1c5ccacd95983e19dff291794e8391c.title: Simultaneous Jackson certificate
244def8ad1c5ccacd95983e19dff291794e8391c.body:
There is a universal constant \(A>0\) such that, for every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) with the following property. Let:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(K\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Rectangle.)} \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) have \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\le u_{\jmath,x}\), \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge 0\), and positive radii
\[
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}>0
\]
for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(P_{x,K}\) be the tensor Jackson polynomial associated with \(\epsilon\), \(K\), and \(Q_x\) in \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}. Then the same polynomial satisfies all of the following conclusions:
\[
\deg_{\jmath}(P_{x,K})\le 2(K-1)
\qquad\text{for every }\jmath\in\mathcal J .
\]
For every \(v\in Q_x\),
\[
\left|P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)\right|
\le
C_\epsilon
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left\{
\frac{\sqrt{(v_{\jmath}-\ell_{\jmath,x})(u_{\jmath,x}-v_{\jmath})}}{K}
+
\frac{r_{\jmath,x}}{K^2}
\right\}.
\]
There are a finite multi-index set \(\mathcal A_x\) and coefficients \(b_{x,\alpha}\) such that, for every \(v\),
\[
P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}
b_{x,\alpha}
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left(\frac{v_{\jmath}-b_{\jmath,x}}{r_{\jmath,x}}\right)^{\alpha_{\jmath}},
\]
with
\[
\alpha_{\jmath}\le 2(K-1)
\qquad\text{for every }\alpha\in\mathcal A_x\text{ and every }\jmath\in\mathcal J,
\]
and
\[
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}|b_{x,\alpha}|
\le
A^K(1+\epsilon^{-1})
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x}.
\]

041bd46c498db45ef586164279fff40795693d70.title: Normalized coefficient envelope
041bd46c498db45ef586164279fff40795693d70.body:
Let \(\epsilon>0\) be the overlap parameter from \(\cref{obj:ass:fixed-overlap}\), let \(K\ge2\) be an integer, and let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a rectangle over the four outcome-arm coordinate set \(\mathcal J\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Ordered endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\le u_{\jmath,x}\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative lower endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Positive radii.)} With
\[
b_{\jmath,x}=\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\]
one has \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(b_x=(b_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\), let \(r_x=(r_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\), and let \(P_{x,K}\) be the Jackson tensor polynomial attached to \(Q_x\) by \(\cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}\). Define
\[
\mathcal R_{x,K}(z)
=
P_{x,K}\bigl((b_{\jmath,x}+r_{\jmath,x}z_\jmath)_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\bigr)
-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x} b_{x,\alpha}\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} z_\jmath^{\alpha_\jmath},
\]
where \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is the global cell extension from \(\cref{obj:def:global-extension}\) and \(\mathcal A_x=\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})\). Then
\[
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}|b_{x,\alpha}|
\le
(2^{60})^{K}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}.
\]
Moreover, every \(\alpha\in\mathcal A_x\) satisfies
\[
\alpha_\jmath\le 2(K-1)
\]
for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).

624fb2e7389820911c15abd2215b323624f75a77.title: Jackson tensor extraction
624fb2e7389820911c15abd2215b323624f75a77.body:
Using the four outcome-arm coordinate set \(\mathcal J\) of \cref{obj:ass:fixed-overlap}, let \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), let \(K\) be an integer, and let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a four-coordinate rectangle with centers and radii as in \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}:
\[
b_{\jmath,x}=\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(K\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Lower endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge 0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap parameter.)} \(\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Radii.)} \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist a polynomial \(P_{x,K}\) in the four physical coordinates and a polynomial \(\mathcal R_{x,K}\) in the four normalized coordinates such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Physical degree.)} Every coordinate degree of \(P_{x,K}\) is at most \(2(K-1)\).
\item \textbf{(Normalized degree.)} Every \(\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})\) satisfies \(\beta_\omega\le 2(K-1)\) for each coordinate \(\omega\).
\item \textbf{(Centered evaluation.)} For every four-coordinate vector \(v\),
\[
P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\mathcal R_{x,K}\left(\left\{\frac{v_\jmath-b_{\jmath,x}}{r_{\jmath,x}}\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right).
\]
\item \textbf{(Jackson convolution.)} For every angle vector \(\vartheta:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
P_{x,K}\left(\left\{b_{\jmath,x}+r_{\jmath,x}\cos(\vartheta_\jmath)\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right)
\]
equals the order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution of \(\bar f_\epsilon\) precomposed with the affine parametrization of \(Q_x\), evaluated at \(\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Coefficient envelope.)}
\[
\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})}\left|(\mathcal R_{x,K})_\beta\right|
\le
2^{40K+20}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}.
\]
\end{itemize}

1855c80461f109d9193c4a3d81b043b458484af0.title: Dense moment matching construction
1855c80461f109d9193c4a3d81b043b458484af0.body:
For \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), a dense domain certificate
\[
2\le d,\qquad
0<\epsilon,\qquad
\epsilon<\frac12,\qquad
0<a_{n,d}\le \frac12,
\]
and a dense prior family \(K\mapsto(\nu_{0,K},\nu_{1,K})\) with its moment-matching certificate at every positive even degree \(K\), the dense moment-matching construction is the object with the following components:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dense law.)} For each \(\theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\), \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) is the potential-outcome probability law induced by the dense full-data cell masses.
\item \textbf{(Approximation scale.)}
\[
K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil 4L_d\rceil,\qquad
E_K=\inf\left\{e\in\mathbb R:\exists p,\ \deg(p)\le K\ \text{and}\ 
\forall t\in[-1,1],\ \bigl||t|-p(t)\bigr|\le e\right\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Poisson intensity and amplitude.)}
\[
\lambda_{n,d}=\frac{2n}{d},\qquad
a_{n,d}=\sqrt{\frac{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}{64\lambda_{n,d}}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Coordinate priors.)} The two coordinate priors are
\[
\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}},\qquad \nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Dense product priors.)} The priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\) are obtained by restricting \(\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) and \(\nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) to \([-1,1]^d\), scaling each coordinate by \(a_{n,d}\), and mapping into the dense contrast class.
\item \textbf{(Observation mixtures.)} The mixtures \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) are the observation-kernel mixtures induced by \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\), with independent Poissonized sample size \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\).
\item \textbf{(Risk and separation.)} The risk component is \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}\), and the prior target-mean separation component is
\[
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
E_{\Pi_{1,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
-
E_{\Pi_{0,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}.
\]
\end{itemize}
The construction also carries the supplied prior-pair certificate at degree \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\) and the identities
\[
K=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}},\qquad
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}.
\]

e1ad9be88ec14ee89777c848e98b92a1bc816351.title: Equal-propensity L1 reduction
e1ad9be88ec14ee89777c848e98b92a1bc816351.body:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), let \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), let \(\mathbb P_0\) be an observed law on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), and let \(\mu_n\) be a law on \(n\) observed triples. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} The law \(\mu_n\) is the \(n\)-fold product law generated by \(\mathbb P_0\), as in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}.
\item \textbf{(Alphabet size.)} \(2\le d\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap range.)} \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every pair \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), let
\[
\mathbb P=\operatorname{Obs}\{\mathrm{L1Emb}(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\},
\]
where \(\operatorname{Obs}\) is the observed margin from \cref{obj:def:observed-margin} and \(\mathrm{L1Emb}\) is the \(L_1\) embedding from \cref{obj:synth_6}. The law \(\mathbb P\) belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}, and, for every \(x\in[d]\),
\[
p_x=\frac{P_x+Q_x}{2}.
\]
Moreover, whenever \(p_x>0\),
\[
\pi_x=\frac12,
\]
and the observed-law optimal-regression value from \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value} satisfies
\[
\Psi(\mathbb P)=\frac12+\frac14\sum_{x\in[d]} |P_x-Q_x|.
\]
Finally, the explicit fixed-\(n\) product Markov kernel obtained by applying the single-observation \(L_1\) embedding kernel independently across the \(n\) coordinates transforms the fixed paired-sample law generated by \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\) exactly into the product law \(\mathbb P^{\otimes n}\). Consequently, for the fixed-sample minimax squared risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk},
\[
\frac{1}{16}\,\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\le \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon},
\]
where \(\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\) is the normalized two-sample \(L_1\) minimax mean-squared risk.

\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}.
\]

a974c18b1f8157e2050e1d166cedfd2ffc2fb70f.title: Dense moment-matching construction
a974c18b1f8157e2050e1d166cedfd2ffc2fb70f.body:
For \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), the overlap parameter, a dense domain certificate
\[
2\le d,\qquad
0<\epsilon,\qquad
\epsilon<\frac12,\qquad
0<a_{n,d}\le \frac12,
\]
and a dense prior family \(K\mapsto(\nu_{0,K},\nu_{1,K})\) indexed by positive even degrees, define the dense moment-matching construction as follows.  For every positive even \(K\), the family carries the prior-pair conditions that \(\nu_{0,K}\) and \(\nu_{1,K}\) are probability measures supported on \([-1,1]\), are symmetric, have matching moments through degree \(K\), and satisfy
\[
\int_{-1}^1 |t|\,d\nu_{1,K}(t)
-
\int_{-1}^1 |t|\,d\nu_{0,K}(t)
=
2E_K .
\]
The construction has components:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dense law.)} For each \(\theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\), \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) is the potential-outcome law induced by the dense full-data masses, equivalently \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), \(\mu_{1x}=(1+\theta_x)/2\), and \(\mu_{0x}=(1-\theta_x)/2\), with \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) conditionally independent Bernoulli variables given \(X=x\), \(A\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of the potential outcomes, and \(Y=Y(A)\).
\item \textbf{(Approximation scale.)} The approximation degree and best even-degree approximation error are
\[
K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil4L_d\rceil,
\qquad
E_K=\inf\left\{e\in\mathbb R:\exists p,\ \deg(p)\le K,\ 
\sup_{t\in[-1,1]}\bigl||t|-p(t)\bigr|\le e\right\}.
\]
The construction uses \(E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}\).
\item \textbf{(Poisson intensity and amplitude.)} The one-cell Poisson intensity and dense contrast amplitude are
\[
\lambda_{n,d}=\frac{2n}{d},
\qquad
a_{n,d}=\sqrt{\frac{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}{64\lambda_{n,d}}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Coordinate priors.)} The coordinate priors are
\[
\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}},
\qquad
\nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Dense product priors.)} The priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\) are the pushforwards into the dense contrast class of the restrictions of \(\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) and \(\nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) to \([-1,1]^d\), under coordinatewise scaling by \(a_{n,d}\).
\item \textbf{(Observation mixtures.)} The mixtures \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) are the observation-kernel mixtures induced by \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\), with independent Poissonized sample size \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\).
\item \textbf{(Risk and separation.)} The risk component is the Poissonized minimax risk
\[
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}.
\]
The prior target-mean separation is
\[
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
E_{\Pi_{1,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
-
E_{\Pi_{0,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}.
\]
\end{itemize}
The construction carries the supplied prior-pair certificate at degree \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\) and the identities
\[
K=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}},
\qquad
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}.
\]

7b4f3699d0b4e10321380523311d4f8ec0e03b5e.title: Tensor Jackson modulus
7b4f3699d0b4e10321380523311d4f8ec0e03b5e.body:
Let \(D\) be a finite coordinate dimension, let \(K\) be a positive integer, and let \(f:\mathbb R^D\to\mathbb R\). Let \(L\ge0\), let \(a_i\ge0\) and \(b_i\ge0\) for each \(i\in[D]\), and fix an angle vector \(\varphi\in\mathbb R^D\). Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Kernel.)} The order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution is formed from the order-four Jackson kernel in \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}.
\item \textbf{(Continuity.)} The function \(f\) is continuous on the normalized cube \([-1,1]^D\).
\item \textbf{(Weighted increment modulus.)} For every shift \(\tau\in\mathbb R^D\),
\[
\left|f\{\cos(\varphi-\tau)\}-f(\cos\varphi)\right|
\le
L\sum_{i=1}^D\left(a_i|\tau_i|+b_i\tau_i^2\right),
\]
where cosine is applied coordinatewise.
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\left|(\mathcal J_K f)(\cos\varphi)-f(\cos\varphi)\right|
\le
L\sum_{i=1}^D\left(\frac{32a_i}{K}+\frac{64b_i}{K^2}\right).
\]
