2^{40K+20}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}.
\]
\end{itemize}

4e3dd34d95e532cdc18bbba4606bea8a91bec1c1.title: Jackson tensor extraction
4e3dd34d95e532cdc18bbba4606bea8a91bec1c1.body:
Using the overlap-parameter notation of \cref{obj:ass:fixed-overlap}, let \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), let \(K\) be an integer, and let
\(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a four-coordinate rectangle with
\[
b_{\jmath,x}=\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(K\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Lower endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge 0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap parameter.)} \(\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Radii.)} \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist a polynomial \(P_{x,K}\) in the four physical coordinates and a polynomial
\(\mathcal R_{x,K}\) in the four normalized coordinates such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Physical degree.)} Every coordinate degree of \(P_{x,K}\) is at most \(2(K-1)\).
\item \textbf{(Normalized degree.)} Every \(\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})\) satisfies
\(\beta_\omega\le 2(K-1)\) for every coordinate \(\omega\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Centered evaluation.)} For every four-coordinate vector \(v\),
\[
P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\mathcal R_{x,K}\left(\left\{\frac{v_\jmath-b_{\jmath,x}}{r_{\jmath,x}}\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right).
\]
Here \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is the globally defined cellwise maximum contribution from
\cref{obj:def:global-extension}.
\item \textbf{(Jackson convolution.)} For every angle vector \(\vartheta:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
P_{x,K}\left(\left\{b_{\jmath,x}+r_{\jmath,x}\cos(\vartheta_\jmath)\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right)
\]
equals the order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution from \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel} of
\(\bar f_\epsilon\) precomposed with the affine parametrization of \(Q_x\), evaluated at
\(\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Coefficient envelope.)}
\[
\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})}
\left|(\mathcal R_{x,K})_\beta\right|
\le
2^{40K+20}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}.
\]
\end{itemize}

a846e5c1726259ecf7fb8d77bc4ce30782f67cb2.title: Tensor Jackson coefficient envelope
a846e5c1726259ecf7fb8d77bc4ce30782f67cb2.body:
With the Jackson kernel notation of \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}, assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Order.)} \(K\ge 1\) is an integer.
\item \textbf{(Function.)} \(f\) is continuous on the normalized cube \([-1,1]^{\mathcal J}\), where \(\mathcal J\) is the four arm-outcome coordinate set.
\item \textbf{(Envelope.)} \(B\ge 0\) and \(\lvert f(z)\rvert\le B\) for every \(z\in[-1,1]^{\mathcal J}\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exists a polynomial \(\mathcal R\) in the four normalized coordinates such that, for every angle vector \(\varphi:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
\mathcal R(\cos\varphi)
=
\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^{\mathcal J}}
f\{\cos(\varphi-\tau)\}
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}J_K(\tau_\jmath)\,d\tau .
\]
Here cosine is applied coordinatewise. Moreover, every multi-index \(\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R)\) satisfies
\[
\beta_\omega\le 2(K-1)
\qquad\text{for every }\omega\in\mathcal J,
\]
the total degree of \(\mathcal R\) is at most \(8(K-1)\), and its coefficient one-norm satisfies
\[
\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R)}
\lvert \mathcal R_\beta\rvert
\le 2^{40K+20}B .
\]

groups.title: Equal-propensity normalized \(L_1\) embedding
groups.body: For \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), \(\mathrm{L1Emb}(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\) is the full-data law on \((X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\) with covariate mass \(p_x=(P_x+Q_x)/2\), treatment propensity \(\pi_x=1/2\), outcome regressions \(\mu_{1x}=P_x/(P_x+Q_x)\) and \(\mu_{0x}=Q_x/(P_x+Q_x)\) on cells with \(P_x+Q_x>0\), conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes with these means, treatment drawn independently of the potential outcomes given \(X\), and observed outcome \(Y=Y(A)\). Equivalently, its observed margin has cell masses \(q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=P_x/4\) and \(q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=Q_x/4\), with a consistency-compatible completion.

groups.title: Fixed-sample two-sample \(L_1\) minimax risk
groups.body: Let \((Z_i,W_i)_{i=1}^n\) be independent paired observations with \(Z_i\sim\mathbf P\), \(W_i\sim\mathbf Q\), and \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\). The normalized two-sample \(L_1\) minimax mean-squared error is \[ \mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}:=\inf_{\widehat D}\sup_{(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2}E_{\mathbf P,\mathbf Q}\left[\left\{\widehat D((Z_i,W_i)_{i=1}^n)-\|\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\|_1\right\}^2\right], \] where the infimum is over all measurable real-valued functions of the paired sample.

groups.title: Dense Poisson observation kernel
groups.body: For \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(d\ge2\), \(\operatorname{Obs}_{n,d}\) is the Markov kernel from dense contrasts \(\theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\) to finite observed samples that maps \(\theta\) to the law of an independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\) number of observations from \(\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\). Thus, for any prior on \(\theta\), composing the prior with \(\operatorname{Obs}_{n,d}\) gives the corresponding Poissonized observed-sample mixture.

groups.title: One-cell dense likelihood ratio
groups.body: Fix a Poisson cell intensity \(\lambda\ge0\). Let \(R_+\) and \(R_-\) be the two sign counts in one dense cell, and let \(E_0\) denote expectation under the zero-contrast baseline law \(R_+,R_-\stackrel{\mathrm{ind}}{\sim}\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda/2)\). For \(\theta\in[-1,1]\), the one-cell likelihood ratio relative to this baseline is \[ L_\theta(R_+,R_-):=(1+\theta)^{R_+}(1-\theta)^{R_-}. \] In the dense lower bound, \(L_{\theta_x}\) applies this definition with the cell contrast \(\theta_x\) and \(\lambda=\lambda_{n,d}\).

groups.title: Dense moment-matching construction
groups.body:
For \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), a domain certificate \(2\le d\) and \(0<a_{n,d}\le 1/2\), and a dense prior family \(K\mapsto(
u_{0,K},
u_{1,K})\) satisfying the stated moment-matching certificate at every positive even degree, define \(\operatorname{DenseMean}_{n,d,\epsilon}\) to be the dense moment-matching experiment consisting of the dense laws \(P_	heta^{\mathrm{dense}}\), the lower-bound degree \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil4L_dceil\), the intensity \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), the amplitude \(a_{n,d}=\sqrt{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}/(64\lambda_{n,d})}\), the coordinate priors \(
u_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}\) and \(
u_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}\), their scaled product priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\) on \([-a_{n,d},a_{n,d}]^d\), the induced Poissonized observation mixtures \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) with independent total sample size \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\), the Poissonized risk \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}\), and the prior target-mean separation \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}=E_{\Pi_{1,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_	heta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}-E_{\Pi_{0,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_	heta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}\).

groups.title: Dense likelihood tail
groups.body: For the dense lower-bound degree \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\), Poissonized cell intensity \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), and dense amplitude \(a_{n,d}\), define the dense likelihood tail by \[\operatorname{tail}_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}:=\sum_{r=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}^{\infty}\frac{(\lambda_{n,d}a_{n,d}^2)^r}{r!}.\]

groups.title: Good-pilot event
groups.body: Fix a cell \(x\), four-cell mass vector \(q_x=(q_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\), Poisson scale \(m>0\), alphabet logarithm \(L_d=\log(ed)\), pilot-radius constant \(H_0\), and pilot counts \((N'_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\). Put \(c_{\jmath,x}=N'_{\jmath,x}/m\) and \(h_{\jmath,x}=H_0\{\sqrt{c_{\jmath,x}L_d/m}+L_d/m\}\). The coordinatewise good-pilot event used for the pilot rectangle is \[\mathsf G_x:=\bigcap_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\left\{\left|\frac{N'_{\jmath,x}}{m}-q_{\jmath,x}\right|\le \frac{h_{\jmath,x}}{4}\right\}.\]

groups.title: Interval projection
groups.body: For real numbers \(a\leq b\), let \(\Pi_{[a,b]}:\mathbb R\to [a,b]\) be the interval projection \(\Pi_{[a,b]}(z)=\min\{b,\max\{a,z\}\}\).

groups.title: Total variation distance
groups.body: For probability laws \(\mathbb M_0\) and \(\mathbb M_1\) on a common measurable space, define \(\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb M_0,\mathbb M_1)=\sup_{B}\lvert \mathbb M_0(B)-\mathbb M_1(B)\rvert\), where the supremum ranges over measurable events \(B\).

groups.title: Tensor Jackson convolution on $Q_x$
groups.body:
Let $0<\epsilon<1/2$, let $K\ge 2$ be an integer, and let $Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]$ have center $b_{\jmath,x}=(\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x})/2$ and positive radius $r_{\jmath,x}=(u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x})/2$ in each coordinate. Let $J_K(t)=c_K\{\sin(Kt/2)/\sin(t/2)\}^4$ on $[-\pi,\pi]$, with removable values filled continuously and with $c_K$ chosen so that $\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}J_K(t)\,dt=1$. The tensor Jackson convolution of $\bar f_\epsilon$ on $Q_x$ is the function $\mathsf J_{\epsilon,K,Q_x}$ defined by
\[
\mathsf J_{\epsilon,K,Q_x}(b_x+r_x\odot\cos\theta)
:=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^{\mathcal J}}\bar f_\epsilon\{b_x+r_x\odot\cos(\theta+t)\}\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}J_K(t_{\jmath})\,dt_{\jmath},
\]
for $\theta\in[-\pi,\pi]^{\mathcal J}$, where products, sums, cosine, and multiplication by $r_x$ are taken coordinatewise over $\mathcal J$.

groups.title: Dense prior target mean
groups.body: For \(j\in\{0,1\}\), define the dense prior target mean by \[ \mathrm{Mean}_{j,n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}} := E_{\theta\sim\Pi_{j,n,d}}\,\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}. \] Here \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) is the equal-mass dense law indexed by \(\theta\), \(\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\) is its observed margin, and \(\Pi_{j,n,d}\) is the corresponding scaled product prior on dense contrasts.

groups.title: Tensor Jackson convolution operator $\mathcal J_K$
groups.body: For a positive integer $K$, let $J_K(t)=c_K\{\sin(Kt/2)/\sin(t/2)\}^4$ on $[-\pi,\pi]$, with the removable values filled in continuously and with $c_K$ chosen so that $\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}J_K(t)\,dt=1$. For a finite coordinate dimension $D$ and a function $f:\mathbb R^D\to\mathbb R$, the order-$K$ tensor Jackson convolution is the operator $\mathcal J_K$ defined, for $\theta\in\mathbb R^D$, by \[ (\mathcal J_K f)(\cos\theta) := \int_{[-\pi,\pi]^D} f\{\cos(\theta+t)\}\prod_{i=1}^D J_K(t_i)\,dt, \] where cosine and addition are coordinatewise. Equivalently, the product kernel $\prod_{i=1}^D J_K(t_i)$ is normalized to have integral one over $[-\pi,\pi]^D$.

synth_3.title: Fixed-law squared risk
synth_3.body: For an estimator \(\widehat V\) based on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) and an observed law \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), define \[ \operatorname{Risk}_{\mathbb P}(\widehat V,\Psi):=E_{\mathbb P^{\otimes n}}\left[\left\{\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\Psi(\mathbb P)\right\}^2\right], \] where \(\mathbb P^{\otimes n}\) denotes the law of \(n\) independent observations each distributed as \(\mathbb P\).

synth_4.title: Causal minimax risk
synth_4.body: For \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge2\), and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), write \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)^{\otimes n}\) for the law of \(n\) independent observations each distributed as the observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\), and define the observed-sample causal minimax squared risk by \[ \mathfrak R^{\mathrm{causal}}_{n,d,\epsilon}:=\inf_{\widehat V}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}} E_{\operatorname{Obs}(P)^{\otimes n}}\left[\left\{\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-V^\star(P)\right\}^2\right], \] where the infimum is over all measurable maps from \(([d]\times\{0,1\}^2)^n\) to \(\mathbb R\).

synth_5.title: Pilot-failure contributions
synth_5.body: Fix a cell \(x\), a four-cell mass vector \(q_x\), Poisson scale \(m>0\), and Jackson tuning. Let \(\mathbb P_{m,q_x}^{\mathrm{pil,eval}}\) denote the product-Poisson law of the pilot and evaluation count vectors, and let \(\mathsf G_x\) be the coordinatewise good-pilot event used for the pilot rectangle in the Jackson--factorial construction. With \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\) denoting the clipped cell statistic built from the pilot and evaluation counts, define \[ \mathrm{PF}_{1,x}:=\int_{\mathsf G_x^c}\left|T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)\right|\,d\mathbb P_{m,q_x}^{\mathrm{pil,eval}}, \qquad \mathrm{PF}_{2,x}:=\int_{\mathsf G_x^c}\left(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)\right)^2\,d\mathbb P_{m,q_x}^{\mathrm{pil,eval}}. \]

synth_6.title: Equal-propensity normalized \(L_1\) embedding
synth_6.body: For \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), \(\mathrm{L1Emb}(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\) is the full-data law on \((X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\) with covariate mass \(p_x=(P_x+Q_x)/2\), treatment propensity \(\pi_x=1/2\), outcome regressions \(\mu_{1x}=P_x/(P_x+Q_x)\) and \(\mu_{0x}=Q_x/(P_x+Q_x)\) on cells with \(P_x+Q_x>0\), conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes with these means, treatment drawn independently of the potential outcomes given \(X\), and observed outcome \(Y=Y(A)\). Equivalently, its observed margin has cell masses \(q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=P_x/4\) and \(q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=Q_x/4\), with a consistency-compatible completion.

synth_7.title: Fixed-sample two-sample \(L_1\) minimax risk
synth_7.body: Let \((Z_i,W_i)_{i=1}^n\) be independent paired observations with \(Z_i\sim\mathbf P\), \(W_i\sim\mathbf Q\), and \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\). The normalized two-sample \(L_1\) minimax mean-squared error is \[ \mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}:=\inf_{\widehat D}\sup_{(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2}E_{\mathbf P,\mathbf Q}\left[\left\{\widehat D((Z_i,W_i)_{i=1}^n)-\|\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\|_1\right\}^2\right], \] where the infimum is over all measurable real-valued functions of the paired sample.

synth_9.title: One-cell dense likelihood ratio
synth_9.body: Fix a Poisson cell intensity \(\lambda\ge0\). Let \(R_+\) and \(R_-\) be the two sign counts in one dense cell, and let \(E_0\) denote expectation under the zero-contrast baseline law \(R_+,R_-\stackrel{\mathrm{ind}}{\sim}\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda/2)\). For \(\theta\in[-1,1]\), the one-cell likelihood ratio relative to this baseline is \[ L_\theta(R_+,R_-):=(1+\theta)^{R_+}(1-\theta)^{R_-}. \] In the dense lower bound, \(L_{\theta_x}\) applies this definition with the cell contrast \(\theta_x\) and \(\lambda=\lambda_{n,d}\).

synth_11.title: Dense likelihood tail
synth_11.body: For the dense lower-bound degree \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\), Poissonized cell intensity \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), and dense amplitude \(a_{n,d}\), define the dense likelihood tail by \[\operatorname{tail}_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}:=\sum_{r=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}^{\infty}\frac{(\lambda_{n,d}a_{n,d}^2)^r}{r!}.\]

synth_12.title: Good-pilot event
synth_12.body: Fix a cell \(x\), four-cell mass vector \(q_x=(q_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\), Poisson scale \(m>0\), alphabet logarithm \(L_d=\log(ed)\), pilot-radius constant \(H_0\), and pilot counts \((N'_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\). Put \(c_{\jmath,x}=N'_{\jmath,x}/m\) and \(h_{\jmath,x}=H_0\{\sqrt{c_{\jmath,x}L_d/m}+L_d/m\}\). The coordinatewise good-pilot event used for the pilot rectangle is \[\mathsf G_x:=\bigcap_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\left\{\left|\frac{N'_{\jmath,x}}{m}-q_{\jmath,x}\right|\le \frac{h_{\jmath,x}}{4}\right\}.\]

synth_13.title: Interval projection
synth_13.body: For real numbers \(a\leq b\), let \(\Pi_{[a,b]}:\mathbb R\to [a,b]\) be the interval projection \(\Pi_{[a,b]}(z)=\min\{b,\max\{a,z\}\}\).

synth_14.title: Total variation distance
synth_14.body: For probability laws \(\mathbb M_0\) and \(\mathbb M_1\) on a common measurable space, define \(\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb M_0,\mathbb M_1)=\sup_{B}\lvert \mathbb M_0(B)-\mathbb M_1(B)\rvert\), where the supremum ranges over measurable events \(B\).

synth_15.title: Dense contrast law
synth_15.body:
For an integer \(d\geq 2\) and a contrast vector \(\theta=(\theta_x)_{x\in[d]}\) with \(\theta_x\in[-1/2,1/2]\) for every \(x\in[d]\), define \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) as the full-data probability law on \((X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\) whose atom at \((x,a,y,y_0,y_1)\in[d]\times\{0,1\}^4\) is
\[
P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}(x,a,y,y_0,y_1)
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{1}{2d}\, b_{(1-\theta_x)/2}(y_0)\, b_{(1+\theta_x)/2}(y_1),
& y=y_a,\\[0.8em]
0,
& y\neq y_a,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(y_a=y_1\) if \(a=1\) and \(y_a=y_0\) if \(a=0\), and \(b_\mu(1)=\mu\), \(b_\mu(0)=1-\mu\).

synth_18.title: Treatment-outcome coordinate set
synth_18.body:
The treatment-outcome coordinate set \(\mathcal J\) is
\[
\mathcal J:=\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}.
\]
A coordinate index is denoted by \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).

synth_20.title: Tensor Jackson convolution operator $\mathcal J_K$
synth_20.body: For a positive integer $K$, let $J_K(t)=c_K\{\sin(Kt/2)/\sin(t/2)\}^4$ on $[-\pi,\pi]$, with the removable values filled in continuously and with $c_K$ chosen so that $\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}J_K(t)\,dt=1$. For a finite coordinate dimension $D$ and a function $f:\mathbb R^D\to\mathbb R$, the order-$K$ tensor Jackson convolution is the operator $\mathcal J_K$ defined, for $\theta\in\mathbb R^D$, by \[ (\mathcal J_K f)(\cos\theta) := \int_{[-\pi,\pi]^D} f\{\cos(\theta+t)\}\prod_{i=1}^D J_K(t_i)\,dt, \] where cosine and addition are coordinatewise. Equivalently, the product kernel $\prod_{i=1}^D J_K(t_i)$ is normalized to have integral one over $[-\pi,\pi]^D$.
